client_brief:
Recover three apparel graphics and prove they survive small reproduction

Cordwain has lost the working artwork for three overland graphics. We need a vector specialist who can recover what is actually in the references and make a useful garment-ready family, not deliver an unchecked automatic trace.

What we need back
- Recovered garment mark: 3 named exports. The geometry follows the authoritative source mark: the graphic's own flat web export, or its bench sample photograph where one exists, with nothing added that neither shows. The lettering is faithful to the source: it carries every word of the graphic's own flat web export, spelled as there, drawn as in its source and not reset in the brand type system.
- Garment graphics application sheet: 1 named export. Placement scale matches the supplied garment constraints: each graphic sits where it printed on its bench sample or on the printer submission sheet, no wider than the brand sheet's maximum print width for that graphic, its hoodie badge width for a badge and otherwise the width for its placement. The specified ink count is respected: no graphic is specified in more than three inks.
- Garment lookbook layout: 1 named export. The garment and graphic relationship is visible for each of the three recovered marks. The identity is consistent with the recovered masters.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table.

Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.tagline: Made for the long way round
brand_identity.sector: Mid tier overland and hiking apparel label selling graphic tees and hoodies through its own store and four independent outfitters
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016 in Bend, Oregon; a small independent label, a handful of people, direct to consumer plus four stockists
brand_identity.about: Cordwain Overland makes graphic apparel for people who drive the back roads and walk the ridgelines. Our graphics are the reason people buy: customers zoom in on the print detail before they add to cart. Every drop is a small set of designs printed with care on garments meant to be worn hard.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged twenty four to forty who care how a print is made, can tell a discharge print from a thick plastisol slab, and screenshot the print detail before they buy
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tees at thirty four dollars, hoodies at seventy eight. Mid tier: a clear step above a bargain blank, priced on print quality rather than logo. Two or three tight inks with a bit of texture read as the craft they pay for.

palette.name: Basalt
palette.usage: The workhorse ink (cordwain_brand_sheet.md) in the Compass chest and Ridgeline back marks, and in the Overland badge where it follows overland_badge.png; headings, running copy and spec lines on Bone; the wordmark and its 2 pt rule; the only dark page ground or text panel; a drawn dark garment.

palette.name: Trail Sand
palette.usage: An ink in overland_badge.png and the brand sheet's ink for dark garments; in the sheet and lookbook only ink swatches and thin rules, or a drawn garment of that colour. Never a page ground, text panel or type colour.

palette.name: Pine Shadow
palette.usage: An ink in ridgeline_back.png; in the sheet and lookbook only ink swatches and thin rules, or a drawn garment of that colour. Never a page ground, text panel or type colour.

palette.name: Rust Ridge
palette.usage: An ink in compass_chest.png and ridgeline_back.png; in the sheet and lookbook used sparingly, as the brand sheet asks, for ink swatches and thin rules only. Never a page ground, text panel, type colour or drawn garment.

palette.name: Bone
palette.usage: The light page ground and text panels of the application sheet and lookbook, the warm off-white the Cordwain Overland store page uses in cordwain_store_grab_01.png; all type set on Basalt; the brand's light garment colour, for a drawn light garment, and a light ink.

brand_identity.typography: Cordwain Overland runs on GT America Expanded Bold 700 for display and Atlas Grotesk Regular 400 for text, with Atlas Typewriter Regular 400 held back for ink codes. Step 01, display, is GT America Expanded Bold 700 capitals at 34 pt on 37 pt leading, letterspaced from about 0.060 em until the two lines of the badge optically justify to the identical measure: CORDWAIN directly over OVERLAND, split by a 2 pt Basalt rule the full width of the block, and the same setting runs at 44 px on 48 px on screen. Step 02, subheading, is the same face in capitals at 18 pt on 20 pt leading tracked 0.020 em for drop and product heads, set on one line and never letterspaced to justification. Step 03, body, is Atlas Grotesk Regular 400 at 10 pt on 13.5 pt leading, tracking zero, set to a maximum of 65 characters. Step 04, fine print, is Atlas Typewriter Regular 400 at 8.5 pt on 12 pt leading tracked 0.030 em, carrying ink counts, colour names, placement and maximum print widths. The stack never becomes one line.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plainspoken and a little dry; we talk about how a thing is made, not how it will change your life. Example line the brand would write: "Three tight inks, printed to last the season."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The brand sheet is two pages of internal notes: the palette in words, the placement rules we have always used, our maximum print widths for chest and full back, and a paragraph on what we mean by a tight print. Our old designer worked off site and we never got the layered files; for three of our best selling graphics all that survives is a few flat web exports and two printed samples we photographed on the bench.
brand_identity.values: The print is the product. We would rather run two or three honest inks with real texture than a muddy multi colour job, and we never price the line out of its own customers.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: The wordmark is always a two line stack, CORDWAIN directly over OVERLAND, both lines letterspaced until they optically justify to the identical measure and split by a 2 pt Basalt rule the full width of the block.

type_system.tagline: Made for the long way round
type_system.text_face: Atlas Grotesk Regular 400 (Atlas Typewriter Regular 400 for ink codes)

scale.family: GT America Expanded Bold, capitals only
scale.tracking: plus 0.060 em, letterspaced to optical justification
scale.note: The badge lock up. CORDWAIN sits directly over OVERLAND, each line letterspaced until both optically justify to the identical measure, split by a 2 pt Basalt rule running the full width of the block. Tracking is a starting value only: the two lines are spaced to the measure, not to a number. The same setting runs at 44 pt on 48 pt as a screen headline. The stack never becomes one line.

scale.role: Subheading / H2 · drop and product heads
scale.family: GT America Expanded Bold, capitals only
scale.note: Product and section heads on the store, the lookbook and the hang tag. Caps only, one line, never letterspaced to justification: that behaviour belongs to the badge alone.

scale.sample: Three tight inks, printed to last the season.
scale.note: Running copy everywhere: product descriptions, drop notes, stockist pages.

scale.role: Fine print · ink codes and print specs
scale.sample: BASALT · TRAIL SAND · RUST RIDGE · CHEST AND FULL BACK
scale.note: Ink counts, colour names, placement and maximum print widths. Always Atlas Typewriter, never Atlas Grotesk, so a spec reads as a spec.

type_system.signature_move: The wordmark is always a two line stack, CORDWAIN directly over OVERLAND, both lines letterspaced until they optically justify to the identical measure and split by a 2 pt Basalt rule the full width of the block. The squared block registers before the mountain does.
rules: Never break the stack onto one line, at any size, including the 44 px screen headline.
Both lines of the wordmark are letterspaced until they optically justify to the identical measure; the measure wins over any fixed tracking value.
The two lines are always divided by a 2 pt Basalt rule running the full width of the block.
Display is GT America Expanded Bold 700 in capitals only.
Atlas Grotesk Regular 400 carries running copy and nothing else carries it.
Ink codes and print specs are always Atlas Typewriter Regular 400, never Atlas Grotesk.
Optical justification is reserved for the badge lock up; ordinary heads are never letterspaced to a measure.
Two or three tight inks with real texture, never a muddy multi colour job, and never price the line out of its own customers.

palette_rules.distribution: In the application sheet and lookbook, page grounds and text panels are Bone or Basalt and nothing else. On Bone, headings, running copy, spec lines and the wordmark with its 2 pt rule are Basalt; on Basalt, all type is Bone, so the wordmark sits on Bone where its Basalt rule reads. Trail Sand, Pine Shadow and Rust Ridge are for ink swatches and thin rules only, never a type colour, together no more than 5% of the designed area outside the marks, drawn garments and photographs. A drawn garment takes the palette colour of the garment colour it stands for (Bone, Basalt, Trail Sand or Pine Shadow) and is outside the 5% accent cap. In each recovered mark, every fill is one of the inks that graphic's source carries.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph. In the marks every ink is a solid fill; any texture kept from the source is solid ink broken by gaps, never partial opacity, and there is no gradient or halftone, as the printer's sheet requires.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for any page ground, text panel, type, rule, icon, drawn garment or mark fill; no gradient or halftone in any mark; no graphic specified in more than three inks.
palette_rules.photography: Garment photographs keep their own colour and are never recoloured toward the palette: the dark hoodie in cordwain_sample_hoodie_badge.jpg stays dark and the light tee in cordwain_sample_tee_compass.jpg stays light.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
